stem: In the figure, line \(\ell\) is parallel to line \(m\). Which equation must be true?
solution: The angle just below line \(\ell\) on the left side of the transversal corresponds to angle \(b^{\circ}\) (just below line \(m\) on the left), so it also measures \(b^{\circ}\).
That angle and angle \(a^{\circ}\) form a straight angle along the transversal, so \(a + b = 180\).
(Angles \(a^{\circ}\) and \(b^{\circ}\) are same-side exterior angles, which are always supplementary.)

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(360^{\circ}\) is the sum of the angles around a point, not the relationship between these two angles.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This treats the angles as complementary; same-side exterior angles are supplementary.
explanation.C: Correct. Angles \(a^{\circ}\) and \(b^{\circ}\) are same-side exterior angles, so they are supplementary.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Same-side exterior angles are not equal; in the figure one is obtuse and the other is acute.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'B': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'B', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
a=ang('J','F','H'); b=ang('U','E','G')
assert P['J'][1]==P['K'][1] and P['U'][1]==P['V'][1]
assert abs(a+b-180)<0.1 and abs(a-b)>5 and abs(a+b-90)>5 and abs(a+b-360)>5
assert choices[answer]=='\\(a + b = 180\\)'
